title: Part
$comment: Role: the canonical chat part taxonomy (docs/architecture.md §3.1; ocai/chat/types/parts.py). One document = one Part in omit-absent wire form. The `type` tag is an OPEN string vocabulary: known canonical tags dispatch to a variant subschema via if/then; a tag this revision does not know matches no branch and still validates (that payload decodes to PartUnknown — total decode, never a raise). This file also hosts the shared $defs (envelope, providerRef, source, span, annotation, cacheHint) that message.schema.json and chat_request.schema.json reference.
description: One canonical content part: a tagged union on `type`, kept open through the part registry. Every part carries the universal optionals `id` (stable part identity), `anchor` (a ProviderRef to provider-side state), and `cache_hint`, plus the common IR envelope.

type.description: The open part discriminator. Known canonical tags: text, image, audio, video, document, reasoning, tool_call, tool_result, server_tool_call, server_tool_result, refusal, opaque (plus the placeholder `undefined`). Plugins register namespaced tags (e.g. "anthropic.mid_conv_system"). Unknown tags are LEGAL: readers decode them to PartUnknown, preserving the payload verbatim.

envelope.$comment: The common IR envelope (ocai/core/ir.py IRObject) every canonical object carries. Omit-absent: unset optionals and empty bags are never emitted; schemas therefore never require them.

version.description: The canonical IR revision this object conforms to — a dated tag on the `ocai` interface (e.g. "2026-07"). Never the library semver, never a provider interface tag: the three version axes stay distinct.

provider_options.description: Request passthrough, namespaced by destination interface (e.g. key "openai.chat_completions"). A codec expands only its own namespace; foreign namespaces are never forwarded.

extensions.description: The namespaced bag for unmapped-but-preserved provider data (e.g. key "openai.logit_bias"). Censused: every key's value schema is registered in spec/extensions/; an unregistered key is a CI failure.

providerRef.$comment: ocai/core/refs.py ProviderRef — a name for state living on a provider's side. The scoped honesty rule: interface-scoped refs (the default) are UNSUPPORTED crossing any other (provider, interface); provider-scoped refs survive same-provider sibling-interface crossings unreported (an OpenAI file id is valid across chat_completions/responses/batch) and are UNSUPPORTED across providers; model-scoped refs are additionally breakage when the bound resource (qualifier) changes (Gemini cachedContents). Crossing beyond the ref's validity scope is always reported, never silently dropped.

provider.description: The provider that minted the ref (e.g. "openai").

kind.description: Open code for what the ref names. Known canonical values: response_id, file, thought_signature, audio_id. Unknown values are legal and preserved verbatim.

replay.description: Whether the provider requires the ref back on follow-ups. Open code; known values: optional (useful context), required (dropping it produces a 400 on replay — weighted as breakage, not mere loss).

scope.description: The ref's validity boundary. Open code; known values: interface (valid only within the minting (provider, interface) — the default when omitted), provider (valid across the provider's sibling interfaces, e.g. OpenAI file ids), model (bound to one resource below the interface, e.g. Gemini cachedContents). Unknown values are legal, preserved verbatim, and read as interface-scoped — the narrowest, most honest boundary.

qualifier.description: The bound resource for model-scoped refs (e.g. the model a Gemini cachedContent was minted against); omitted for wider scopes.

cacheHint.$comment: ocai/chat/types/config.py CacheHint [provisional] — a per-part prompt-caching marker (Anthropic cache_control is the model).

ttl.description: Requested cache lifetime as an open provider-shaped token (e.g. "5m", "1h"); absent means the provider default.

span.$comment: ocai/chat/types/annotations.py Span — a half-open character range [start, end) in Unicode code points of the decoded text.

end.description: The exclusive end offset; end >= start.

extensions.description: Preserved unknown span fields and invalid offset evidence; invalid evidence never establishes attribution.

pointer.description: JSON Pointer within that result payload; empty names the root. Never resolved implicitly.

annotation.$comment: ocai/chat/types/annotations.py Annotation — one span-anchored citation carried by a text part, never a side channel.

kind.description: Open citation kind, including url_citation; unknown values are preserved.

span.description: The text range being attributed; absent when the provider cited the whole part.

url.description: The cited web URL, when the source is a web page.

document_index.description: Zero-based index of the cited request document, when the source is caller-supplied material.

file.description: The provider-side file handle backing the citation, when the source is an uploaded file.

title.description: Human-readable title of the cited source.

cited_text.description: The verbatim excerpt the provider quoted, when given.

opaque.description: Provider-opaque citation state (e.g. an encrypted grounding token) riding along verbatim to keep the citation replayable.

source.$comment: ocai/core/sources.py Source union — where media bytes live. An open tagged union like Part: known tags dispatch via if/then; unknown tags are legal (SourceUnknown preserves them verbatim).

mime_type.description: The media MIME type, when known.

url.description: The URL of the remote media.

mime_type.description: The media MIME type, when known.

ref.description: The provider-side file handle (OpenAI file_id, Gemini Files API name, Anthropic Files).

mime_type.description: The media MIME type, when known. Pre-freeze rename from `media_type` (aligning with the base64/url siblings); decoders still accept the old key.

type.description: The open source discriminator. Known canonical tags: base64 (inline payload), url (remote), ref (provider-hosted handle); placeholder `undefined`. Unknown tags are legal and decode to SourceUnknown.

partBase.$comment: The universal optionals every part shares (PartBase), applied to KNOWN and UNKNOWN tags alike, plus the IR envelope.

id.description: The part's stable identity within its message, when the provider (or ocai) assigned one — what lets item semantics (OpenAI /responses) round-trip.

anchor.description: Provider-side state backing this part (an item id, a file handle); inherits ProviderRef's scoped crossing rule — UNSUPPORTED beyond the ref's validity scope.

partText.description: A run of text with its citations anchored on it (PartText).

annotations.description: Span-anchored citations attributing ranges of `text` to sources; they travel with the text through slicing, folding, and conversion.

partMedia.description: An image or audio part: media referenced through the Source union (PartImage / PartAudio).

source.description: Where the media bytes live — inline base64, a URL, or a provider-hosted ref.

partVideo.description: A video part over the Source union, with optional clipping/sampling metadata (PartVideo).

start_offset.description: Where playback/sampling starts, as a provider-shaped duration token (e.g. "20s"), verbatim.

end_offset.description: Where playback/sampling ends; same form as start_offset.

fps.description: The frame-sampling rate requested for the model.

partDocument.description: A document part (PDF and friends) over the Source union, with citation-support metadata (PartDocument).

title.description: The document's title, surfaced to the model for citations.

context.description: Caller-supplied context about the document, surfaced to the model but never quoted as content.

partReasoning.description: Model reasoning — ONE merged shape for every provider idiom (PartReasoning): a /responses reasoning item, an Anthropic thinking block, or a Gemini thought is one part each, never two correlated ones.

text.description: The raw reasoning text, when the provider surfaces it.

summary.description: The provider-generated summary of the reasoning, when the interface returns one instead of (or besides) raw text.

signature.description: The provider's integrity signature over the reasoning; replay=required signatures are weighted as breakage when dropped.

opaque.description: Encrypted/opaque reasoning state (OpenAI encrypted_content) that must ride along verbatim.

partToolCall.description: The model's request to invoke a named tool (PartToolCall). args_json is the authoritative wire truth: a verbatim JSON string, parsed on read, compared under the *_json parse-compare rule (spec/canonical-json.md §7).

call_id.description: The id correlating this call with its tool_result sibling. Cross-provider conversion regenerates call ids — recorded as a SemanticShift, never silent.

name.description: The tool name, matching a request Tool.name.

args_json.description: The arguments as the verbatim JSON string the model produced (a partial fragment is legal mid-stream).

status.description: The open tool-call lifecycle code shared with streaming. Known values: input_streaming, input_complete, executing, output_available, output_error. Unknown values are legal and preserved verbatim.

executed_by.description: Who runs the tool. Known values: client (the caller replies with a tool_result), provider (built-in tools; results arrive as server_tool_result). Open code.

partToolResult.description: The caller's answer to a tool_call, correlated by call_id — a sibling in the transcript, never nested inside the call (PartToolResult).

call_id.description: The id of the tool_call this answers.

parts.description: The result content — itself a list of parts, so tools can return text, images, and documents without a parallel content model.

is_error.description: Whether the tool execution failed; the parts then carry the error content.

partServerTool.description: A provider-executed built-in tool invocation or result (PartServerToolCall / PartServerToolResult): a typed spine — kind, id, lifecycle — over a verbatim, byte-faithful payload.

kind.description: The open tool-kind code. Known values: web_search, code_execution, mcp_call. Unknown kinds are legal, preserved verbatim, and remain visible and reportable.

call_id.description: The id correlating the call with its server_tool_result sibling.

status.description: The open lifecycle code shared with tool_call parts. Known values: input_streaming, input_complete, executing, output_available, output_error.

payload.description: The provider's invocation/result payload, verbatim and byte-faithful — never reshaped.

partRefusal.description: A refusal surfaced as content (PartRefusal); pairs with finish.reason == "refusal". Mid-generation refusal is a response; a pre-generation block is a ContentFilterError, not a response.

partOpaque.description: DELIBERATE provider-unique content, census-registered in spec/extensions/ (PartOpaque). Strictly distinct from the PartUnknown decoder fallback: opaque is chosen on purpose by an author or codec; unknown is a future canonical tag this revision cannot name.

kind.description: The namespaced, censused content key (e.g. "anthropic.mid_conv_system"). An unregistered kind is a CI failure.
